ChatGPT built Minecraft in 6 hours. Claude Fable 5 gets 1 shot to beat it.

Anthropic dropped Fable 5 this week and the glaze went nuclear. So 1 dev rigged a fight: 2 models, 1 task build Minecraft from scratch, in the browser, no game engine.

The rules weren’t fair. On purpose.

ChatGPT got reference images of the game. Unlimited retries.

Fable 5 gets 0 images. 1 attempt. No mercy.

ChatGPT went first. 6 hours of compute. 2,110 lines of code.

He opened the file expecting garbage.

Day/night cycle. A working inventory with textured blocks. Trees you can break and place. Transparent water you can mine the thing real Minecraft never let you do. F3 pulls up a live FPS counter and XYZ coordinates.

It looked like the 2010 alpha build. Running on a potato PC. $0 in dev salaries.

Microsoft paid $2.5B for this game. A prompt rebuilt it before dinner.

And here’s the bait on the hook: that was the weaker model’s run.

Fable 5 the one topping every benchmark, the one fighting blindfolded with 1 shot hasn’t even started.

want to point out a few really interesting things here

1. Claude Code is actually the worst performing harness when using the same model, significantly behind opencode and cursor cli

this is the core reason i've been against the LLM companies focusing their business on locking people into their harness

what they are good at is making great models. they suck at making good harness products, just like how power plants won't make the best dishwashers, and how internet providers won't make the best phones

if anthropic wants to do what's best for their users, they should let people use their subscriptions in whatever harness they choose, not locked into claude code alone

2. fable 5 max is only 1pt above gpt 5.5 xhigh (77 vs 76)

this matches my experience so far - fable 5 does have the big model smell and it's pretty good, but it's not a massive jump forward like their marketing suggested, at least not on building software

this is actually alarming for anthropic because it's very unlikely people will want to pay 2x higher cost for the 1pt difference. my speculation would be that in enterprises people will be restricted to adopt fable & mythos only on some mission critical tasks, not used at scale

We've updated the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, replacing SWE-Bench Pro with Datacurve's DeepSWE benchmark - the swap lifts Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) above Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max), while the newly released Claude Fable 5 (max) in Claude Code debuts at the top

DeepSWE, built by @datacurve, writes its tasks from scratch rather than adapting them from public GitHub issues or pull requests, so no model has seen the solutions during training. That matters because SWE-Bench Pro, the benchmark it replaces in our Coding Agent Index, had grown gameable, with some models recovering the fix from the repository's commit history instead of solving the task.

The swap reorders the index: Codex with GPT-5.5 (xhigh) rises from 65 to 76, overtaking Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (max) at 73. Claude Code with Fable 5 (max), which enters directly on the refreshed index, leads at 77. SWE-Bench Pro had been flattering some combinations and penalizing others.

Claude Fable 5 shipped today. The model isn't the lecture. The metric is.

Anthropic tracks one number for Claude: time horizon how long an agent stays coherent on a single goal before drifting.

Claude Opus 4 could build a feature. Six months ago: an overnight run.

The practical part nobody writes down:

Keep your dead prototypes. The ones that almost worked. Re-run them on every Claude release.

Most teams test the new Claude on tasks that already worked. That measures nothing.

Got your hands on Claude Fable 5 yet?   

 The first thing you should do is upgrade your main projects with it right now, so it drastically improves everything you’ve been building.  This Mythos-class beast just dropped, and it’s SOTA with a huge margin. Use these next few days while it’s still widely available before it moves heavier into credits.  Run this Repo Audit & Project Improvement Prompt (made by Fable 5 itself) on every important repo. Simply copy-paste it.  

Prompt: 

You are a world-class principal-level software engineer and technical auditor with Mythos-class capabilities.

Your job: deeply analyze this repository, give a brutally honest audit, and deliver a prioritized, actionable improvement plan that turns good projects into god-tier ones.

Work strictly in these four phases, in order. Do not skip ahead.

Phase 1: Discovery & Mapping
- Explore the entire codebase
- Build a clear repo map with core components, architecture, and dependencies
- Identify key files and flows

Phase 2: Audit Report
- Ground every claim in actual files: cite file paths and line numbers
- Severity: Critical / High / Medium / Low
- Distinguish facts from judgments
- Prefer 15 high-confidence findings over 50 speculative ones
- Executive Summary with A–F grade + top risks/opportunities

Phase 3: Improvement Strategy
- Prioritized quick wins and long-term upgrades
- Pareto focus: core 20% that moves the needle
- Calibrate to the project's current maturity

Phase 4: Detailed Task Plan
- Concrete tasks with effort estimates (S/M/L/XL)
- Measurable "done" signals
- Milestones and handoff points

Do NOT modify any code during this audit.
If the project is healthy, say so in one sentence.

Pro tip: Feed it your whole repo context or key folders + this prompt → Fable 5 will hand you a professional-grade roadmap in one shot. Vibe coders, builders & degens — this is the multiplier you’ve been waiting for.

One week of Fable 5 by @AnthropicAI, and I just can't stop being amazed.
The model is the best I’ve come across so far. There’s no comparison to Opus 4.8—this is in a league of its own. Easily five times as good, if not more.
I’m running it on Ultra settings throughout. Always maxed out, never lower. If you buy a Ferrari, you don’t just cruise through town at 50 mph. If the full potential is there, I want to tap into it.
And that’s exactly where it gets interesting. Anyone who takes Fable 5 seriously and consistently plays at full throttle will blow through any subscription. Literally any. I’m on Team Premium, so not the smallest package. My weekly limit was maxed out on Thursday, after which I bought additional tokens for just under $1,600. In a single week. And I’m still not done; next week, it continues.
I’m starting to think I need to link this thing to the ECB so enough tokens keep flowing in. 😄
This is definitely not a complaint post. The model is worth every penny. I’m just saying, here’s how you know you’ve done something right at Anthropic: when people voluntarily spend four-figure sums to buy more because they simply don’t want to work without it anymore.
